title: Product Material Lab: Paint Budget Allocator
description: A product design workstation where users manage a fixed 'paint budget' across a ShaderBall preview sphere and a ToyCar model. Users allocate color channels (R, G, B), metalness, and roughness between the two objects under a conservation constraint — increasing a property on one object must decrease it on the other. Full undo/redo history tracks every adjustment.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load ShaderBall.glb on the left and ToyCar.glb on the right, both on a neutral gray infinite-plane ground. Use a three-point lighting rig with an HDR-style environment map approximation (PMREMGenerator with a RoomEnvironment or simple gradient). Camera starts at a 3/4 angle viewing both objects.

Core mechanic: A conserved 'Paint Budget' system. There are 5 sliders in an HTML overlay panel: Red (0-1), Green (0-1), Blue (0-1), Metalness (0-1), Roughness (0-1). Each slider is a coupled dual-thumb range: the left thumb controls the ShaderBall's value, the right thumb controls the ToyCar's value, and they must always sum to exactly 1.0. Dragging one thumb automatically adjusts the other to maintain conservation. Display numeric readouts for both objects beside each slider.

Interaction steps: (1-2) Adjust Red and Green channels for ShaderBall, ToyCar auto-compensates. (3-4) Adjust Blue and Metalness on ToyCar side. (5-6) Fine-tune Roughness split. (7) Click 'Swap All' button to mirror all values between objects in one action. (8-9) Use Undo button (Ctrl+Z supported) to revert the swap, then Redo (Ctrl+Y). (10-11) Click directly on either model to select it, highlighting it with an outline pass or emissive boost, then use a 'Copy Material To Other' button that sets the other object to matching values while still respecting conservation by setting both to 0.5. (12) A 'Randomize' button that randomly distributes all five channels while maintaining each sum at 1.0.

Apply MeshStandardMaterial properties in real time. Store full state history as an array of snapshots for undo/redo with a max depth of 50. Show a step counter and current budget totals. Add subtle turntable auto-rotation toggle button.
